nodes.label: Same-value collection equality
nodes.description: A map must decide whether NaN and signed zero identify one key or several.

nodes.label: Equality and hash consistency
nodes.description: A hash table can fail to find an equal key when the equality and hash policies disagree.

nodes.label: Unknown and NULL comparison
nodes.description: A missing database value cannot safely be treated as an ordinary known value in every predicate.

nodes.label: Stable entity identity
nodes.description: A database row moves or is replaced, yet clients need a durable identifier for the same business entity.

nodes.label: Structural equality
nodes.description: Independent values representing the same data should compare equal without sharing an allocation.

nodes.label: Floating-point exceptional equality
nodes.description: Scientific values include NaN and signed zero, so ordinary equal and total sortable order answer different questions.

nodes.label: Coercive equality
nodes.description: Inputs arriving as strings and numbers invite convenient comparisons but can silently change types during comparison.

nodes.label: Custom comparison protocols
nodes.description: A domain type needs ordering without implementing each relational operator independently and inconsistently.

nodes.label: Reference identity
nodes.description: A graph algorithm must distinguish two different nodes that happen to contain equal data.

nodes.label: Equality equivalence laws
nodes.description: A set's deduplication behavior becomes incoherent when equal is not reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

nodes.label: Unicode canonical equivalence
nodes.description: Visually matching text can use different code-point sequences and fail a direct string comparison.

nodes.label: Total ordering
nodes.description: A sorted index needs consistent ordering between every pair and agreement between ordering and equality.

nodes.label: Interning and canonical representatives
nodes.description: Repeated equal strings waste storage or repeated comparison effort, but arbitrary object identity is not value equality.

nodes.label: Mutable hash keys
nodes.description: A key changes after insertion and no longer hashes or compares as it did when assigned a bucket.
